title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff and circuit breaker to prevent regional thrashing
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context: Production incident (2026-02-18) where the SLO enforcer's aggressive backoff and immediate regional failover looped under partial GPU pool degradation, causing cascading capacity churn and elevated tail latency. Reproduction: load test with 40% simulated instance loss + synthetic traffic with mixed short/long sequences reproduces thrash within 5-10 minutes. Root cause: two concurrent issues: 1) backoff schedule reset on transient success causing cooldown to be shorter than intended; 2) circuit breaker state transitions were evaluated independently per-region without considering global enforcement signals, causing simultaneous failover and re-attach thrashing. Change summary: - Implement exponential backoff state machine with persistent cooldown key (TTL=10m) stored in enforcer state store to avoid immediate backoff reset on single successful request. - Add global coordination flag for regional circuit breaking: when a region trips, we mark a global soft-failover window (configurable) to prevent other regions from performing immediate reciprocal failover/attach. - Introduce a conservative-load-shedding threshold during enforcer cooldown to preferentially shed best-effort traffic classes (embeddings, non-blocking batch jobs) before shedding low-latency requests. - Add feature flag rollout (feature.slo.enforcer.stable-backoff) and an escape hatch (api: /admin/enforcer/disable-hotfix) for emergency rollback. - Add unit and integration tests that simulate regional loss and ensure state persists across short success spikes. Checklist: [x] tests added and passing locally; [x] feature flag gated; [x] metrics emitted for backoff_state and global_failover_window; [x] canary deployed to staging and us-west; [x] manual rollback verified. Risk/rollback: gated behind feature flag, default off for controlled rollout. Rollback via feature flag or admin endpoint; migration is non-destructive (TTL-based key), no DB schema changes. Related: ENG-2104, incident SUP-9842.
